## Decisions and gates

### Project bootstrap, staged build, and first launch

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Architecture.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Onboarding.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:CMakeLists.txt`
- Reusable claim: A game consumes an exact Engine revision through staged configure, bake, build, and launch milestones with generated outputs kept non-authoritative.
- Decision: Current Engine guides and examples own the reusable workflow; project presets, binaries, ports, and subconfigs stay external.
- Promotion gate: Engine-owned starter and tutorials pass their declared clean-host lanes.

### Engine submodule update reconciliation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`
- Reusable claim: An Engine pin change requires a complete incoming-range audit, generated contract comparison, project integration review, and retained safety state until validation completes.
- Decision: The Engine owns reusable reconciliation; each game owns its integration consequences and evidence.
- Promotion gate: The Engine procedure remains executable without either project checkout.

### Generated content ownership and dependency order

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/GuiSystem.md`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`
- Reusable claim: Source metadata, authored resources, generators, baking, and runtime outputs form an ordered ownership graph; generated output is repaired at its source.
- Decision: Reusable ordering is Engine-owned; project generators and concrete outputs retain project ownership.
- Promotion gate: Every generated artifact names its source, generator, validation order, and stale-output signal.

### Script modules, lifecycle, authority, and concurrency

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Events.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Properties.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Multithreading.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ScriptStyle.md`
- Reusable claim: Module initialization, callback side, entity covers, async/yield invalidation, events, properties, and generated bindings need explicit ownership and validation.
- Decision: Engine lifecycle and binding mechanics are promoted; game module maps, events, remotes, properties, and lock groups remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Claims are tied to Engine callback/export source and focused lifecycle or synchronization tests.

### Script and native nullability

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `fonline-tla:Nullability.md`
- Reusable claim: Nullable script handles and native pointer annotations require one source-backed vocabulary, diagnostics, and analyzer workflow.
- Decision: The Engine guide, compiler diagnostics, and native-boundary checks are normative; TLA migration notes and Last Frontier analyzers remain evidence only.
- Promotion gate: Compiler diagnostics and native-boundary checks enforce the reusable contract; declaration-parity and style analyzers remain explicitly project-owned.

### Native extensions and project-local dependencies

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/NativeExtensions.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ProjectThirdPartyMaintenance.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:SourceExt`
- Reusable claim: Role-scoped project C++ sources, optional hooks, generated exports, vendored patches, and platform/package guards need explicit source and compatibility ownership.
- Decision: Roles, hooks, and binding rules are Engine-owned; SDK integrations and vendored project libraries stay external.
- Promotion gate: The Engine-owned sample compiles and exercises a role-scoped extension at an exact revision.

### Prototype authoring and validation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Prototypes.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Items`
- Reusable claim: Prototype discovery, identity, inheritance, property applicability, references, migration, and strict values are parser-owned contracts.
- Decision: Grammar and built-in properties are Engine-owned; ids, custom metadata, balance, and directory policy stay project-owned.
- Promotion gate: The generated model derives built-in types and properties from current Engine sources.

### Map authoring, baking, and materialization

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/MapAuthoring.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Maps`
- Reusable claim: Map sections, placement identity, ownership, mapper round-trip, side-specific baking, and runtime materialization need one parser-backed contract.
- Decision: Format and tool mechanics are Engine-owned; map kits, quests, encounters, and level-design policy stay external.
- Promotion gate: Mapper, baker, loader, and materialization sources agree with generated reference and focused tests.

### Text packs, languages, and runtime lookup

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Localization.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Texts/Game.engl.fotxt`
- Reusable claim: Text-pack syntax, duplicate variants, ordered language normalization, prototype text, lookup, and renderer color tags are Engine contracts.
- Decision: Engine format behavior is promoted; language priority, semantic keys, lexems, pack catalogs, and authored text remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Current parsers, bakers, script methods, and renderer behavior back every format claim.

### Models, animation timing, and sprite root motion

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/CharacterGenerator.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/TEMPLATE_HumanAnimations.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/CR_HumanMaleNormal.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/VH_Jagger.fo3d`, `last-frontier:Resources/CrittersArt/Critters/VH_Snowmobile.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Docs/Animation.md`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBMob.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBWeapon.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/_VBHuman.fo3d`, `fonline-tla:Resources/VanBuren/art/critters/VbDog.fo3d`
- Reusable claim: Current model grammar, named animation tuples, include templates, tuple AnimSpeed, one-step aliases, exact temporary geometry exceptions, typed durations, 2D frame offsets, movement phase, and stop-time offset normalization must be re-derived from Engine bakers and runtime rather than legacy assets or historical documentation names.
- Decision: Engine mechanics are promoted. Last Frontier's named-template composition is current project evidence; its 3D *_RM import boundary does not prove 2D offset values. TLA's bare AnimEqual, model-level Speed, raw_ptr, and LoadAnimation names are explicit legacy migration evidence, not current alias, tuple-speed, pointer, or loader contracts. No current authored 2D root-motion asset was observed in either pinned project snapshot, so project offset values and gait-quality claims stay non-normative.
- Promotion gate: Current parser/baker/runtime sources, focused duration and geometry tests, and visible representative assets replace historical token and implementation-name assumptions.

### Effects, images, sprites, and shader resources

- Sources: `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Resources/Visual/Effects`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`, `fonline-tla:Resources`
- Reusable claim: Effect state/resources, image inputs, FOFRM composition, baked sprites, factories, atlases, and caches require source-backed format and runtime references.
- Decision: Formats and runtime are Engine-owned; concrete effects, ScriptValue slots, resource precedence, and visual acceptance stay external.
- Promotion gate: Baker and runtime models remain current across every claimed renderer/profile.

### Particle authoring, baking, tools, and runtime

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Particles.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:Resources`
- Reusable claim: SPARK and Effekseer are independent optional authoring/runtime paths with explicit baking, bounds, renderer, Mapper, and validation contracts.
- Decision: Engine backend mechanics are promoted; particle catalogs, textures, budgets, and art direction stay project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Both enabled backends pass source, bake, runtime, tool, and visible integration gates.

### Fonts, audio, and video presentation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/GuiSystem.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:Resources`
- Reusable claim: Font descriptors/layout, supported audio decoders/playback, and Ogg/Theora video paths require separate Engine contracts and visible or audible project acceptance.
- Decision: Engine formats/runtime are promoted; catalogs, typography, mastering, subtitles, licensing, and acceptance stay external.
- Promotion gate: Source and native fixtures back capability claims; each project validates shipped assets on every claimed platform.

### Mapper, AnimationViewer, and ParticleViewer

- Sources: `last-frontier:CMakeLists.txt`, `last-frontier:.vscode/tasks.json`, `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/MapAuthoring.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Particles.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/CharacterGenerator.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `last-frontier:Scripts/MapperRender.fos`, `last-frontier:Tools/MapPreview/generate_map_preview.py`, `fonline-tla:README.md`
- Reusable claim: Interactive tool controls, persistence, resource mounting, outputs, recovery, and visible review evidence need Engine-owned manuals.
- Decision: Stock tool behavior is Engine-owned; Last Frontier demonstrates project tasks, single-process headless map-preview orchestration, warmup and view plans, developer packaging, assets, and layered acceptance, while the TLA README supplies historical compatibility evidence for a project-owned Mapper target and negative evidence because it has no focused-viewer or reusable capture workflow.
- Promotion gate: The stock tools launch against an Engine-owned fixture and changed controls are visibly exercised.

### Client and server profiling

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Profiling.md`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ReanimationPlan.md`
- Reusable claim: Profiling needs exact tool/version matching, one measured process, reproducible workloads, source zones, export interpretation, and evidence boundaries.
- Decision: Profiling mechanics are Engine-owned; scenes, runners, thresholds, and reports stay project-owned.
- Promotion gate: At least one representative Engine-owned capture proves native and script zones with exact tools.

### Reusable gameplay and integration test harness

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Testing.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ReanimationPlan.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`
- Reusable claim: Games benefit from deterministic fixture setup, boundary-based test selection, narrow-first execution, timeout/log contracts, and cross-layer integration evidence.
- Decision: Engine now owns boundary-based test selection plus process readiness, marker, deadline, cleanup, and report semantics. Script test registries, game fixtures/assertions, filters, content, persistence backends, platform labs, and acceptance thresholds stay project-owned.
- Promotion gate: The project-neutral runner has deterministic positive/failure/timeout coverage, a synthetic fixture, and real baked headless server/client proof in Minimal Multiplayer.

### Native and script safety analyzers

- Sources: `last-frontier:Tools/SmartPointerAudit`, `last-frontier:Tools/ExceptionSafetyAudit`, `last-frontier:Docs/Testing.md`, `fonline-tla:Nullability.md`
- Reusable claim: Nullability, smart-pointer, exception-safety, thread-safety, and local-variable policies need Engine-owned contracts and source-backed enforcement boundaries; whole-tree analyzers and baselines remain project-owned until promoted with reusable tests.
- Decision: Engine contracts and in-repository compiler/runtime checks are normative; whole-tree analyzers, project wrappers, allowlists, and integration baselines stay project-owned until promoted into Engine with tests.
- Promotion gate: Engine documents name exact source/runtime/compiler evidence and distinguish reusable checks from embedding-project analyzers, allowlists, and baselines.

### Project generators, formatters, and content audits

- Sources: `last-frontier:Tools/InterfaceEditor`, `last-frontier:Tools/DialogAudit`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:FormatSource.bat`
- Reusable claim: Generated-file discipline and source-level validation are reusable patterns, but concrete project generators and audits are not automatically Engine tools.
- Decision: Engine documents the ownership pattern; the current GUI/dialog generators, formatters, and audits remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Move reusable implementation and tests into Engine before adding any concrete format or command to Engine documentation.

### Dialog tree parser, baker, runtime, editor, and audit

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Dialogs.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/DialogAudit`, `fonline-tla:Dialogs`
- Reusable claim: Both games have dialog content, but the current schema, parser, baker, runtime, editor, and audit are not reusable Engine components.
- Decision: Do not invent an Engine .fodlg contract from project code or authored files.
- Promotion gate: Revisit only after a project-neutral dialog implementation and focused compatibility tests move into Engine.

### Declarative GUI authoring and screen generation

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/GuiSystem.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/InterfaceEditor`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:Gui`
- Reusable claim: The Engine owns the script GUI runtime, but current declarative file formats, generators, editors, widgets, screens, and styles belong to games.
- Decision: Keep runtime mechanics in Engine docs and declarative authoring in each project.
- Promotion gate: A declarative format becomes an Engine contract only after its parser/generator, fixtures, and compatibility policy are Engine-owned.

### AI observation and control bridge

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/AiControl.md`, `last-frontier:SourceExt/ClientAiBridge.cpp`, `last-frontier:Scripts/AiControl.fos`, `last-frontier:Tools/AiControlMcp/ai_control_mcp.py`, `fonline-tla:Docs/AiControl.md`, `fonline-tla:SourceExt/ClientAiBridge.cpp`, `fonline-tla:Scripts/AiControl.fos`, `fonline-tla:Tools/AiControlMcp/ai_control_mcp.py`
- Reusable claim: Two projects expose AI observation/action bridges, but their schemas, QA commands, MCP adapters, and content semantics are still independently project-owned.
- Decision: Promote only the transport envelope, authorization, bounded command/event lifecycle, reference client, and protocol sample; keep every project's observation schema, action catalog, administrator tools, and MCP namespace project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Keep the generated experimental contract, loopback threat boundary, reference client, malformed-peer tests, protocol smoke, and runnable sample current; a native core listener still requires a separate runtime and security promotion.

### Cross-platform packaging and release evidence

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Architecture.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `last-frontier:.github/workflows/cross-platform-tests.yml`, `last-frontier:.vscode/tasks.json`, `last-frontier:.vscode/launch.json`, `last-frontier:CMakeLists.txt`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/web_runner.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_login_enter_game_web.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_web_token_login_web.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_web_combat_web.py`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:.github/workflows/build.yml`, `fonline-tla:CMakePresets.json`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`
- Reusable claim: Package grammar and capability differ from project-qualified host/target release evidence, artifacts, signing, and deployment.
- Decision: Grammar, current capability, repeatable release procedure, evidence boundaries, and failure routing are documented. The Web guide now separates the build-gated WebGL2 client, stock package/shell/server behavior, WebSocket and browser runtime limits, production hosting, and project browser/release qualification. Last Frontier supplies a required nightly/manual packaged Chromium route with loopback serving, explicit wasm/isolation headers, WebSocket login/token coverage, and a deterministic rendered workload; TLA supplies independent Emscripten presets/settings but no equivalent checked browser-package lane. The Android guide separately covers ARM build gates, source-capable x86, generated Gradle/APK behavior, Wi-Fi ADB, typed server-host launch, debug-key fallback, unsupported native self-update, and project-owned device/store qualification. Last Frontier supplies current ARM64 local workflow and all-ABI nightly build evidence but no official APK artifact; TLA supplies independent settings/presets and ARM build evidence but no device qualification. The Engine packaging fixture and Minimal Multiplayer's own archive/runtime lane are Windows-green, and both native hosts require commit-addressed CI artifacts. The first landed Linux tutorial-package evidence, an exact remotely reachable example pin, immutable external artifact, and owner-authorized publication remain incomplete.
- Promotion gate: Each claimed host/target package is reproduced from a public minimal project with immutable CI evidence and explicit capability limits.

### Updater, secrets, signing, security, and recovery operations

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/AuthLoginFlow.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/SteamIntegration.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Sentry.md`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Tools/CodeSign/README.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/CodeSign/sign_windows.cmd`, `last-frontier:Tools/CodeSign/sign_windows.sh`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/README.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_smoke.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_compat_outdated.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_binary_update.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_outdated_runs.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_resource_pack.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_resource_pack_missing.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_staging_promotion.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_server_missing_payload.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_installed_selector.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_installed_selector_windows.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_postfix_variants.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_server_stages_windows_pdb.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_updater_restart_windows.py`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`
- Reusable claim: Engine updater and host/runtime mechanics are only one part of production delivery: mature projects keep transfer settings environment-specific, validate installed and portable paths with executable package tests, isolate postfix variants, and sign the exact patched runtime bytes served by packaged servers.
- Decision: Updater mechanics, installed/portable and variant acceptance lanes, package-time signing of final patched bytes, secret substitution/redaction/handoff, CI isolation, rotation/revocation, incident routing, process/readiness/rollout/shutdown/rollback, and provider-neutral backup/restore/DR boundaries are promoted. Last Frontier supplies broad executable updater evidence; TLA supplies compatibility/configuration evidence but no equivalent updater pipeline lane, so settings alone are not treated as operational proof. Concrete providers, credentials, environments, retention, RPO/RTO, migrations, and production authority remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Document only reusable Engine boundaries with redacted fixtures; require packaged-server evidence for native update claims; project credentials, providers, environments, and incident policy stay external.

### Persistence, save migration, and compatibility

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/DocumentationMaintenance.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`, `fonline-tla:DbPendingChanges.oplog`
- Reusable claim: Entity persistence, database backends, migration metadata, compatibility versions, backup, rollout, and rollback need separate Engine and project ownership.
- Decision: Engine mechanics plus provider-neutral backup-set, oplog, restore, and drill boundaries are promoted; concrete schemas, migrations, providers, schedules, retention, objectives, credentials, and production operations remain project-owned.
- Promotion gate: Engine storage/migration behavior is source-backed; every game validates its schema/data and recovery path before rollout.

### Gameplay systems, content catalogs, and balance policy

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/GameSystems.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ReanimationPlan.md`, `fonline-tla:Scripts`
- Reusable claim: Quest, combat, economy, AI, faction, survival, and other gameplay systems exercise Engine surfaces but do not define reusable Engine behavior.
- Decision: Keep all gameplay semantics, catalogs, balance, quests, and content acceptance in their game repositories.
- Promotion gate: Promote only a minimal reusable primitive with Engine-owned source/tests; never generalize a game's rule set into Engine documentation.

### Analytics, live operations, support, and product services

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Analytics.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Ops/AGENTS.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`
- Reusable claim: Analytics schemas, support operations, commerce, communications, service providers, and live-ops policy are product concerns rather than Engine contracts.
- Decision: Do not add game operations or service-provider procedures to Engine documentation.
- Promotion gate: Only a provider-neutral Engine primitive with source/tests can be promoted; schemas, credentials, KPIs, and procedures remain product-owned.

### AngelScript style, refactoring, and change batching

- Sources: `last-frontier:AGENTS.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Scripts.md`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Tools/Formatter/format_project.py`, `fonline-tla:Docs/ScriptStyle.md`, `fonline-tla:Docs/Refactoring.md`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`, `fonline-tla:Tools/Formatter/format_project.py`
- Reusable claim: Module ownership, generated-file discipline, narrow change batches, formatter use, and validation-after-refactor recur across projects, but style rules still mix project policy and migration state.
- Decision: Engine owns the enforceable namespace, side/module, formatter, generated-source, mutable-global, attributed-call, batching, and validation baseline. Last Frontier's Test_-only mutable-global/direct-call exceptions and broader project formatter are positive current evidence. TLA's broad production mutable-global allowlist is negative migration evidence, not a reusable default. Project comment language, domain vocabulary, generated formats, migration policy, quality thresholds, and gameplay acceptance remain external.
- Promotion gate: The compact Engine convention is derived from compiler/formatter behavior and Engine CoreScripts, with examples and automated checks independent of project migration plans.

### Documentation localization and terminology governance

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/Localization.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Glossary.md`, `fonline-tla:README.md`
- Reusable claim: Bilingual documentation needs one canonical locale, stable IDs, mirrored routes, terminology ownership, source hashes, code parity, native review, and language-preserving links.
- Decision: The Engine owns its documentation localization process; each game owns player-facing terminology and authored strings.
- Promotion gate: Locale parity, glossary, hash, code-fence, link, search, and native-speaker review gates are explicit before production publication.

### Native, mixed-stack, and AngelScript debugging workflows

- Sources: `last-frontier:.vscode/launch.json`, `last-frontier:.vscode/tasks.json`, `last-frontier:LastFrontier.fomain`, `last-frontier:Docs/BuildAndLaunch.md`, `last-frontier:Docs/Testing.md`, `last-frontier:Tools/CiChecks/check_debug_workflows.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/CiChecks/test_check_debug_workflows.py`, `last-frontier:Tools/PipelineTests/test_crash_diagnostics_linux.py`, `fonline-tla:.vscode/launch.json`, `fonline-tla:.vscode/tasks.json`, `fonline-tla:TLA.fomain`, `fonline-tla:README.md`
- Reusable claim: A production debugging route separates native symbols and debugger semantics, crash-to-log and dump ownership, mixed script/native traces, explicitly enabled loopback AngelScript attach, multi-process selection, live transport capabilities, and focused regression evidence.
- Decision: Last Frontier supplies a strong Windows/Linux native plus AngelScript profile pattern with explicit endpoint enablement, loopback base bind, static validation, and a Linux crash-diagnostic lane. TLA supplies independent compatibility evidence, but its compounds do not explicitly enable the endpoint while its base config disables debugging and uses a wildcard bind; this is negative evidence and not a security or launch template. Engine source and tests remain normative, project target names and incident policy remain external, and the absence of current live endpoint CI is explicit.
- Promotion gate: Every reusable claim is re-derived from Engine source and native tests; project profiles remain exact pinned evidence, and a static editor profile is never promoted to live endpoint qualification.

### Tutorial assets, provenance, and public examples

- Sources: `last-frontier:Docs/ContentWorkflow.md`, `last-frontier:Resources`, `fonline-tla:LICENSE`, `fonline-tla:Resources`
- Reusable claim: Public examples need redistributable minimal assets, exact Engine pins, byte-verified provenance, immutable lesson tags, and pinned/current compatibility evidence.
- Decision: Governance and clean fixtures are Engine-owned; neither project's game assets are copied into public examples without explicit compatible licensing.
- Promotion gate: Every public byte has auditable provenance and each tagged example passes its exact-pin and current-Engine lanes.

## Owner review requirements

| Owner | Scope | Required evidence | Co-review when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `documentation` | Information architecture, stable document identity, ownership, maintenance policy, and publication routing. | manifest and route impact<br>standalone validation<br>generated site and AI delivery freshness | a domain contract changes<br>locale or publication policy changes<br>a public route is added, replaced, or removed |
| `build-release` | CMake, BuildTools, packages, updater distribution, release automation, and reproducible artifacts. | source or executable parser contract<br>affected build, package, or updater check<br>support and migration disposition | platform capability changes<br>runtime ABI or payload changes<br>credentials, signing, or deployment boundaries are involved |
| `runtime` | Applications, entities, lifecycle, persistence, client/server behavior, and runtime compatibility. | owning source and focused tests<br>lifecycle and failure-path analysis<br>migration or compatibility impact where applicable | script bindings or callbacks change<br>network or persistence contracts change<br>platform host behavior changes |
| `scripting` | AngelScript runtime, metadata, generated bindings, callbacks, properties, events, and script contracts. | source metadata or binding model<br>generated API/reference freshness<br>focused compile or runtime test | runtime lifecycle changes<br>network authority or synchronization changes<br>content metadata or migration changes |
| `content-data` | Configuration, baking, authored formats, resources, maps, movement data, and content validation. | parser, baker, or runtime source<br>generated format model/reference freshness<br>representative bake and validation route | rendered or audible output changes<br>tool authoring behavior changes<br>language or terminology behavior changes |
| `frontend` | Rendering, GUI runtime, media presentation, visual resources, input, and client-visible behavior. | owning render or frontend source<br>focused native/runtime check<br>visible or audible acceptance on every claimed profile | platform backend behavior changes<br>content formats or tools change<br>accessibility or localization presentation changes |
| `networking` | Transport, protocol, connection state, authority, synchronization, and compatibility boundaries. | protocol or synchronization source<br>focused multi-endpoint test<br>compatibility and migration disposition | runtime entities or persistence change<br>script remotes or callbacks change<br>security or deployment boundaries change |
| `tooling` | Mapper, editors, viewers, helper command lines, generated tools, and reusable authoring ergonomics. | tool source or executable parser<br>focused structural or interaction test<br>input, output, persistence, and failure contract | content format behavior changes<br>frontend interaction changes<br>platform packaging or availability changes |
| `platform` | Web, Android, host/target toolchains, platform packaging, device behavior, and backend qualification. | toolchain and target source<br>declared build or smoke lane<br>device or browser evidence for runtime claims | package or release policy changes<br>frontend backend behavior changes<br>runtime host assumptions change |
| `quality` | Tests, diagnostics, analyzers, validation policy, reproducibility, and evidence quality. | reproduction or source-backed invariant<br>focused regression or validator<br>clear pass, failure, and residual-risk signals | the owning domain contract changes<br>a gate is weakened or removed<br>manual evidence is used for a production claim |
| `localization` | English/Russian documentation parity, terminology, source freshness, code integrity, and language-preserving delivery. | canonical English source hash<br>glossary and code-fence parity<br>native-language review and locale link/search checks | technical meaning or identifiers change<br>site routing or navigation changes<br>player-facing terminology overlaps project policy |

## Verification

The normal generator/check validates schema, ownership, disposition rules, Engine targets, and deterministic output. A maintainer with both exact external checkouts also runs source verification; it proves every recorded path exists in the pinned commit rather than trusting the current working tree.

```bash
python BuildTools/docs_external_evidence.py --check
python BuildTools/docs_external_evidence.py --check --verify-sources --last-frontier-root ../ --tla-root Workspace/fonline-tla-audit
```
